title: The Ostrich Effect: Your Unopened Statement Costs You

beats.say: The statement you don't open still counts. Every week.
beats.visual: extreme close-up of a sealed bank envelope on a rain-slick table, sodium light reflecting off the paper

beats.say: You skip the app, dodge the mailbox. That's the ostrich effect: avoiding numbers you fear.
beats.visual: silhouette of a person walking past a glowing ATM screen, backlit by neon, low angle

beats.say: Ignoring the balance doesn’t make it disappear. It just lets small problems grow in the dark.
beats.visual: extreme wide shot of a single credit card left on an empty dining table, dim overhead light

beats.say: Most people assume: if I don’t look, I don’t owe. But the money’s still moving.
beats.visual: high angle shot of a phone face-down on a cold fluorescent desk, ashtray nearby

beats.say: A $3,000 card at 24% paying minimums costs $4,887 in interest. Ignorance is expensive.
beats.visual: extreme close-up of a crumpled receipt in a back pocket, blue hour lighting

beats.say: Reality check: the longer you wait, the bigger the hole. Time turns blind spots into sinks.
beats.visual: silhouette of a person standing under a highway overpass, fog rolling in

beats.say: Here’s the move: two minutes, same day each week, open the app.
beats.visual: hands typing on a laptop in a dark room, single practical light casting shadows

beats.say: See the real number. Then decide. Knowledge shrinks the fear.
beats.visual: empty parking lot at night, a single streetlamp illuminating a discarded coffee cup

beats.say: Two minutes a week beats 15 years of surprise interest. That’s the math.
beats.visual: tower edge at dusk, wind tugging at papers on the ledge

beats.say: Start this week. Open the app. The number’s already there. Now you know.
beats.visual: extreme close-up of a finger hovering over a phone screen, low-angle sodium glow

beats.say: Follow for the money rules nobody taught you.
beats.visual: ridge line against a stormy sky, a lone figure walking away

caption: Your bank app won’t judge you. Ignorance will. #MoneyPsychology #OstrichEffect #PersonalFinance #DebtFreeJourney
